sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Hygiene & Nutrition** is the foundational branch of applied biology focusing on personal cleanliness, sanitation, and the study of macro/micronutrients essential for human life.
Relevant throughout the human lifecycle, with critical intervention windows during **prenatal development**, **infancy**, **childhood**, and **adolescence**.
Studied by educators, scientists, and health workers; examined comprehensively under the **UP Assistant Teacher (Science)** recruitment syllabus.
Prevents **deficiency diseases**, enhances **cognitive development**, boosts **immunity**, and maintains personal/public **sanitation standards**.
Encompasses **balanced diet pyramids**, **calorific requirements**, **water-soluble/fat-soluble vitamins**, **deficiency symptoms**, and **pathogenic sanitation**.
Divided into **Macronutrients** (Carbohydrates, Proteins, Fats) and **Micronutrients** (Vitamins, Minerals); and **Personal vs. Environmental Hygiene**.
High-scoring section in the UP Assistant Teacher exam featuring direct conceptual, chemical name, and deficiency-based questions.
Based on the laws of conservation of energy, biochemical synthesis, germ theory of disease, and preventive sanitation.

items.title: 1. The Balanced Diet & Calorific Requirements
items.content:
• **Definition:** A diet containing adequate amounts of all necessary nutrients required for proper growth and functioning.
• **Energy Yield:** **Carbohydrates** (~4.1 kcal/g), **Proteins** (~4.1 kcal/g), and **Fats** (~9.3 kcal/g).
• **Adult Requirement:** Average sedentary man requires **2000-2500 kcal/day**; average woman requires **1800-2000 kcal/day**.
• **Mnemonic for Macronutrients:** **C-P-F** (**C**ars **P**rovide **F**uel - Carbs, Proteins, Fats).

items.title: 2. Fat-Soluble Vitamins (A, D, E, K)
items.content:
• **Vitamin A (Retinol):** Essential for vision; deficiency causes **Nyctalopia** (night blindness) and **Xerophthalmia**.
• **Vitamin D (Calciferol):** Regulates calcium absorption; deficiency causes **Rickets** in children and **Osteomalacia** in adults.
• **Vitamin E (Tocopherol):** Acts as an antioxidant; deficiency causes **sterility** and red blood cell hemolysis.
• **Vitamin K (Phylloquinone):** Essential for blood clotting; deficiency leads to **hemorrhage**.
• **Mnemonic for Fat-Soluble Vitamins:** **ADEK** (Pronounced like 'A-Deck' -> Vitamins stored in fatty deck/liver).

items.title: 3. Water-Soluble Vitamins (B-Complex and C)
items.content:
• **Vitamin B1 (Thiamine):** Deficiency causes **Beriberi**.
• **Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin):** Deficiency causes **Ariboflavinosis** (cheilosis, glossitis).
• **Vitamin B3 (Niacin):** Deficiency causes **Pellagra** (the 4 D's: Diarrhea, Dermatitis, Dementia, Death).
• **Vitamin B12 (Cyanocobalamin):** Contains cobalt; deficiency causes **Pernicious Anemia**.
• **Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid):** Deficiency causes **Scurvy** (bleeding gums).
• **Mnemonic for B-Complex Order:** **T**he **R**at **N**ibbles **P**anecakes **B**efore **C**limbing **F**ast (**T**hiamine, **R**iboflavin, **N**iacin, **P**antothenic acid, **B**iotin, **C**obalamin, **F**olic acid).

items.title: 4. Mineral Deficiencies and Metabolic Roles
items.content:
• **Iron (Fe):** Essential component of **hemoglobin**; deficiency causes **Microcytic Anemia**.
• **Iodine (I):** Required for **thyroxine** hormone synthesis; deficiency causes **Goiter** and **Cretinism**.
• **Calcium (Ca):** Needed for bone matrix and muscle contraction; deficiency causes **tetany** and osteoporosis.
• **Fluorine (F):** Prevents dental caries; excess causes **fluorosis** (mottling of teeth).

items.title: 5. Personal and Environmental Hygiene
items.content:
• **Personal Hygiene:** Practices like handwashing, oral care, bathing, and nail clipping to prevent microbial load.
• **Environmental Hygiene:** Proper disposal of solid waste, sewage treatment, vector control (mosquitoes, flies), and safe drinking water.
• **Water Purification:** Processes include **sedimentation**, **filtration**, **chlorination**, and **boiling** to eradicate waterborne pathogens like *Vibrio cholerae*.

items.title: 6. Protein-Energy Malnutrition (PEM)
items.content:
• **Kwashiorkor:** Caused by severe protein deficiency with adequate caloric intake; marked by **edema** (swelling), potbelly, and thin hair.
• **Marasmus:** Caused by simultaneous deficiency of proteins and total calories; marked by severe muscle wasting, emaciated appearance, and **no edema**.

items.definition: Use sentence: '**R**ath **C**he **T**ffee **P**ar' -> **R**etinol (A), **C**alciferol (D), **T**ocopherol (E), **Phylloquinone** (K).

Use sentence: '**R**hyme **N**ot **P**erfect, **B**ut **C**atch **F**ish' -> **R**iboflavin (B2), **N**iacin (B3), **P**antothenic Acid (B5), **B**iotin (B7), **C**obalamin (B12), **F**olic Acid (B9).
Remember **K**washiorkor has **K**iDney/belly swelling (**edema**), whereas **M**arasmus means **M**uscle wasting with zero fat and zero swelling.
Remember **C**-**T**-**H**-**J** -> **C**holera, **T**yphoid, **H**epatitis A, **J**aundice. All prevented by boiling water and chlorination.
Use phrase: '**PVT TIM HALL**' -> **P**henylalanine, **V**aline, **T**ryptophan, **T**hreonine, **I**soleucine, **M**ethionine, **H**istidine, **A**rginine, **L**eucine, **L**ysine.
Remember the 4 Ds: **D**iarrhea, **D**ermatitis, **D**ementia, and finally **D**eath.

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Kwashiorkor and Marasmus symptoms
items.definition: Students often think both have swelling. **Kwashiorkor** features edema (fluid retention in belly/limbs due to protein lack), whereas **Marasmus** shows extreme emaciation without edema due to total starvation.

items.term: Mistake 2: Storing Water-Soluble vs Fat-Soluble Vitamins
items.definition: Remember that **Fat-Soluble (A, D, E, K)** vitamins can be stored in the liver and adipose tissue causing hypervitaminosis, whereas **Water-Soluble (B-complex, C)** are excreted via urine and must be replenished daily.
Vitamin C (**Ascorbic Acid**) is extremely sensitive to heat and is easily destroyed during prolonged cooking or boiling.
Do not assume carbohydrates yield more energy than fats. **Fats provide more than double** the energy (~9.3 kcal/g) compared to carbohydrates (~4.1 kcal/g).
Students confuse iron with cobalt. **Vitamin B12 (Cyanocobalamin)** uniquely contains **Cobalt** metal, while **Hemoglobin** contains **Iron**.
Comprises all six essential nutrients: **Carbohydrates, Proteins, Fats, Vitamins, Minerals, and Water** in correct proportions.
Provide structural components and energy; subdivided into **Carbohydrates** (sugars/starches), **Proteins** (amino acid polymers), and **Lipids** (fats/oils).
Required in minute amounts for enzymatic regulation; includes **Vitamins** (organic cofactors) and **Minerals** (inorganic ions).
Vital for synthesis of **rhodopsin** in retinal rod cells; deficiency leads to night blindness.
Acts functionally as a **hormone** synthesized in human skin upon exposure to **Ultraviolet-B (UV-B)** radiation.
Acts as a potent reducing agent and is essential for **collagen synthesis** and wound healing.
Iron deficiency leads to **microcytic hypochromic anemia**, while Vitamin B12 deficiency leads to **pernicious megaloblastic anemia**.
Inadequate dietary iodine causes compensatory enlargement of the thyroid gland, known as **endemic goiter**.
Addition of **chlorine tablets** or bleaching powder (**CaOCl2**) disinfects drinking water by releasing hypochlorous acid.
A precise mix of **sodium chloride, potassium chloride, glucose, and trisodium citrate** used to treat fatal dehydration from diarrhea.

upscNotes.content: Memorize the chemical names of all major vitamins alongside their deficiency diseases as UP Assistant Teacher exams frequently ask direct matching-type questions.
Questions often mix up Kwashiorkor and Marasmus regarding the presence of edema. Always remember: edema is present ONLY in Kwashiorkor.
Pay special attention to water treatment chemicals and processes (chlorination, sedimentation) as questions linking hygiene to public health appear regularly.
Do not confuse the energy values of fats and carbohydrates. Fats yield more than double the calories per gram compared to carbohydrates.

keyTakeaways: Balanced diet includes carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water in appropriate ratios.
Fat-soluble vitamins are A, D, E, and K; water-soluble vitamins are B-complex and C.
Vitamin B1 deficiency causes Beriberi, Vitamin C causes Scurvy, and Vitamin D causes Rickets.
Kwashiorkor is due to protein deficiency (with edema), whereas Marasmus is due to protein-calorie starvation (without edema).
Iron deficiency causes anemia, while iodine deficiency causes goiter.
Chlorination and boiling are standard chemical and physical methods for ensuring water hygiene.
Vitamin B12 uniquely contains the trace metal Cobalt.
